lowered.reason: Memory is not unbounded. `listing(commit, deadline, listingLimit)` at state-tree.ts 326-327 stops git at 64 MiB of listing and returns `TipSize.unlisted()` past it. That caps the entries `#sizes` can see at roughly 1M, not an arbitrary count. The path also needs a tip pushed past the entry limit by a hand push or an older build, which the decision treats as an unusual route. Only diagnostic callers (doctor, `records size`, the round report) reach it, and none of them is a write or a normal read.

verification.reason: The code does what the claim says. `StateTree.size` (state-tree.ts 325-330) never checks `entryLimit`, and `#measure` (310-314) does check it before any size is read. `size` goes straight to `#sizes`, which builds the readable-OID set, the `cat-file --batch-check` stdin and a Map for every entry. The base decision table (2026-11-14-git-record-store-refuses-by-location.md, line 66) says the entry limit bounds the memory for sizes, and `size()` bypasses that. The guideline (state-git.md line 28) says `size()` deliberately answers on a tip past a limit. That makes the bypass intentional, but it does not make the bound hold. I could not trace the memory and deadline figures (hundreds of MB, 20 s in doctor) without a run. The one run that would settle them is `size()` on a synthetic tip of about 1M short-path entries.
